item.description: Over 100,000 euro will be spent on upgrading the footpaths in Elphin this year. Extra traffic has been going through the town recently, due to the upgrade of the N5 between Ballaghaderreen and Scramogue. item.title: Hopes lessons can be learned over Bord Bia dispute
item.description: Local politicians have been reacting to the latest developments in the dispute between the Irish Farmers' Association and Bord Bia. The IFA have called off their 4 week protest at Bord Bia Headquarters after the board agreed to an independent review. Chair Larry Murrin will remain in his role but will step aside from chairing board meetings while the review is carried out. item.title: Popular Boyle pub and off licence put up for sale
item.description: A long-standing local business in Boyle has been put up for sale. Daly’s Public House, along with its off-licence and wholesale licences, is located on Bridge Street in the town. The property is being offered in two distinct lots, giving potential buyers flexibility depending on how they want to use it. item.title: Enoch Burke transferred to Castlerea Prison
item.description: Enoch Burke has been transferred to Castlerea Prison The Irish Independent is reporting that the move to the west Roscommon medium security facility took place on Sunday morning. On January 19th, the High Court ordered that Burke be returned to Mountjoy Prison for a fifth time for repeatedly breaching a court order instructing him not to trespass at Wilson’s Hospital School in Co Westmeath. item.title: Affordable housing development in Longford expected to be opened next year
item.description: It's expected a new affordable housing development in Longford Town will be opened in mid 2027. The 25 home development was officially launched earlier today at Ard Michael on the Ballinalee Road. The price of the new homes are set to range from around €228,220 for a 2-bed terrace to €308, 759 for a 3-bed semi detached house. item.title: Two men due in court over double Longford stabbing
item.description: Two men are due to appear before Longford District Court this afternoon over an alleged serious assault in Longford town. The violent incident occurred in Teffia Park, where two men sustained significant injuries took place on February 9th. The two injured men, one aged in his 20s and the other in his 30s, were rushed to Mullingar Hospital. item.title: Funding sought for local autism support worker
item.description: It's hoped that long-term funding can be secured for two autism support officers in Leitrim following the success of a pilot programme in the county The pilot initiative was established to support autistic young people at critical educational transition points. At this month's meeting of the local authority, Cllr James Gilmartin proposed a motion urging the Minister Norma Foley, to provide sustained financial support for at least two such officers in Sligo-Leitrim. Advertisement The Independent

item.title: Winter vomiting bug outbreak impacting Sligo University Hospital
item.description: The HSE has confirmed that visiting restrictions are in place at Sligo University Hospital, due to high rates of the winter vomiting bug. The hospital is currently dealing with a Norovirus outbreak impacting a number of wards. Visiting restrictions are in place on wards with an outbreak, with visiting restricted to compassionate grounds only and with prior arrangements with Ward manager, in advance.
